headline: Air Quality: Dhaka ranks 9th most polluted city worldwide
summary: The capital city faces severe air pollution levels, placing it among the top 10 most polluted cities globally.
details: Dhaka has been ranked as the 9th most polluted city in the world, highlighting a critical air quality crisis in the capital.
The city's air quality index often reaches hazardous levels, posing significant health risks to millions of residents.
Major contributors to this pollution include vehicle emissions, construction dust, and industrial waste.
Environmental experts call for urgent measures to reduce emissions and improve urban planning to combat the rising pollution levels.

headline: Over 300,000: Trump administration has revoked over 300,000 visas
summary: The US State Department reports a rapid acceleration in visa revocations as part of a sweeping immigration crackdown during Donald Trump's second term.
details: The US State Department announced on Tuesday that the Trump administration has revoked more than 300,000 visas since the start of his second term in January 2025.
This marks a significant increase from the 175,000 revocations reported on August 10, indicating a sharp acceleration in the pace of the crackdown.

State Department spokesman Tommy Pigott stated that the administration has revoked visas at a faster pace than any other administration in history, citing zero tolerance for law-breaking, fraud, or threats to national security.
Rights advocates have condemned the move, claiming the crackdown violates due process and free speech rights while creating an unsafe environment for ethnic minorities.
Specific concerns have been raised regarding the revocation of visas for pro-Palestinian protesters and individuals who made social media comments about conservative commentator Charlie Kirk.
The administration has also implemented tightened social media screening for immigrants and visa applicants and imposed higher fees for certain work visas.

Advocates argue that 'national security' is being used as a pretext to target critics and that isolated fraud cases are being used to broadly target specific immigrant communities, such as Somali Americans in Minnesota.
caption:
Over 300,000 US visas revoked. The Trump administration is canceling visas at a faster pace than any administration in history.

The US State Department announced on Tuesday that the Trump administration has revoked more than 300,000 visas since the start of his second term in January 2025.

This marks a significant increase from the 175,000 revocations reported on August 10, indicating a sharp acceleration in the pace of the crackdown.

State Department spokesman Tommy Pigott stated that the administration has revoked visas at a faster pace than any other administration in history, citing zero tolerance for law-breaking, fraud, or threats to national security.

Rights advocates have condemned the move, claiming the crackdown violates due process and free speech rights while creating an unsafe environment for ethnic minorities.

Specific concerns have been raised regarding the revocation of visas for pro-Palestinian protesters and individuals who made social media comments about conservative commentator Charlie Kirk.

The administration has also implemented tightened social media screening for immigrants and visa applicants and imposed higher fees for certain work visas.

Advocates argue that 'national security' is being used as a pretext to target critics and that isolated fraud cases are being used to broadly target specific immigrant communities, such as Somali Americans in Minnesota.
